Yes, centrifugal is the “fictitious” force you feel pushing you outward. (I think of -fugal, is like fugitive, running away.) Centipetal (like you’re pedaling towards the center) is the real force that is pulling the turning mass off moving in a straight line. In this case, the centripetal force is the internal tension of the dough that keeps pieces of it from flying apart.

Both centripetal and centrifugal forces are real; this is required by Newton's 3rd Law. In fact, spinning pizza dough actually proves that centrifugal force is real: if the dough is stretching outwards there must be a force causing it to do so; said force cannot be directed inwards, the dough isn't shrinking, and it cannot be tangent to the rotation because then the dough would just accelerate without changing shape; for the dough to stretch outwards there must be a force that is directed away from the cntre of rotation - the centrifugal force.

The pizza stone is emphatically not fully preheated just because the oven reaches the preset temperature. What is crucial is that the interior of the stone reach that temperature, not just the surface, and that will take longer.

When the interior of the stone is cooler than the surface, some of the heat from the surface will move towards the interior (to move the stone towards equilibrium), rather than all going into the bottom of the pizza. That’s not effective cooking.

Moreover, and most importantly, what happens to the surface temperature of the stone when you place pizza dough on it? It starts to cool, because the heat from the upper element can no longer reach the surface (the dough is now in the way). So, with each passing second, the amount of heat moving from the stone to the dough will continually decrease. Again, you’re not cooking the bottom of the pizza at 850 degrees.

It is only when the interior of the stone reaches the preset temperature that heat from inside the stone will move outwards and continually replenish the heat that is lost at the surface as the dough absorbs it and cooks.
